condition: Peri-operative diabetes — type 1 diabetes before emergency appendicectomy
summary: 23-year-old man with type 1 diabetes (glargine + aspart) and ultrasound-confirmed acute appendicitis, nil by mouth for emergency laparoscopic appendicectomy; glucose 14.6 mmol/L, ketones 0.8.

inputs.hpi: 24 hours of periumbilical pain moving to the right iliac fossa, anorexia, nausea. Type 1 diabetes since age 11 on insulin glargine 22 units at night and aspart with meals. Took his glargine last night; no aspart today because not eating. Glucose rising.

exam.general: HR 96, BP 126/78, RR 18, SpO2 99% on air, T 37.8°C.
exam.abdomen: Tender at McBurney's point with localised guarding.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Non-compressible 8 mm appendix with hyperaemia; no collection.

guideline.name: CPOC guideline — perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery
guideline.section: SGLT2 inhibitors: omit the day before and the day of surgery, check ketones; sulfonylureas omitted on the day of surgery; people with diabetes early on the list; capillary glucose monitoring; VRIII when more than one meal will be missed or in emergency surgery; type 1 diabetes: never omit basal insulin (continue long-acting insulin, usually at a reduced dose) alongside VRIII
guideline.citation: Centre for Perioperative Care. Guideline for perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery. London: CPOC; 2021 (updated 2022).

rationale: Permutation: type 1 diabetes in emergency surgery. The appendicectomy is correct. Tests VRIII and continuing basal insulin (never omitted).
